original_question: Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. Determine the first-order asymptotic behavior of f(n) itself, not just of ln f(n).
target_in_paper: Section 5, Open Problems, p. 4: the draft is aiming at the paper’s explicit open problem of finding the first-order asymptotic description of f(n) itself, beyond the logarithmic asymptotic already proved in Theorem 3.1.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the same counting function f(n) studied in the paper, namely the number of ordinary integer partitions whose nonzero part-multiplicities are all distinct; it also correctly targets the sharper unresolved problem in the paper, namely obtaining asymptotics for f(n) itself rather than only for ln f(n) [Section 1, p. 1; Section 2, p. 1; Theorem 3.1, p. 1; Section 5, p. 4].
missing_details: It should specify the asymptotic regime explicitly: n is a positive integer and n tends to infinity.
It should make the paper’s notation explicit: T(n) is the set of such partitions and f(n)=|T(n)|.
It should clarify that 'distinct multiplicities' means the positive multiplicities of the part sizes are pairwise distinct; zero multiplicities are ignored.
It should say that the partitions are ordinary integer partitions of n, not weighted, colored, restricted, or generalized partitions.

It should sharpen 'first-order asymptotic behavior' into a stand-alone asymptotic request, e.g. finding an explicit main term A(n) with f(n)~A(n), since the paper already proves only the first-order asymptotic of ln f(n).
refined_question: Let T(n) be the set of ordinary partitions of the positive integer n in which the positive multiplicities of the part sizes are pairwise distinct (the paper’s 'Wilf partitions'), and let f(n)=|T(n)|. Theorem 3.1 shows only that ln f(n)∼(6n)^{1/3}ln((6n)^{1/3}) as n→∞. Determine a first-order asymptotic formula for f(n) itself; that is, find an explicit main term A(n) such that f(n)∼A(n) as n→∞.
justification: The draft does not target the main proved result itself, because Theorem 3.1 already gives the leading asymptotic for ln f(n) [Section 3, p. 1]. Instead, it targets the follow-up open problem stated immediately afterward: Section 5 says that finding the first-order asymptotic description of f(n) itself would be a Herculean task [Section 5, p. 4]. To make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must import the paper’s definitions of Wilf partitions, T(n), and f(n) from Section 1 and Section 2 [pp. 1], and state explicitly that the asymptotic variable is n→∞. No broader variant is introduced in the nearby discussion, so the scope should remain exactly this counting problem for Wilf partitions.
